title: Choose the visual world for DoseGuard
question: The roll assigned the Calendar Blister Pack. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Calendar Blister Pack
options.lineage: pharmacy calendar blister packs: clear domes over printed foil
options.thesis: Today's medicine is a strip of blister pockets you can read at a glance: sealed, due, or popped.
options.viewport: White app shell with a light-blue top bar; Today leads with a large blister strip of the day's doses, the due pocket ringed, one big Get my dose button beneath it.
options.risk: Reads as decoration if the pockets stop carrying real dose state.

raised.raise: The due dose gets one unmistakable ring, and finished doses stay visible as popped pockets, never hidden.
Each dose keeps a fixed cell in the strip; state changes fill or empty it without reflowing anything.
One element dominates each screen: the strip on Today, the single instruction on each dose step.
Type runs on three strict size steps of one face, so hierarchy never relies on decoration.
The text-size control remaps the whole page live, with no component overriding it.

options.label: Weekly Pill Organizer
options.thesis: The day is a row of lidded compartments, morning to night; a lid opens when its dose is due.
options.viewport: Light-blue shell; Today shows morning, noon, evening and night compartments side by side, the due one open with its pill and a big button.
options.risk: The pill organizer is the first thing most medication apps reach for.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and departure boards
options.thesis: Doses ranked by time like departures; a due dose lights up and holds until you act.
options.viewport: Light shell; Today is a departure-style board of dose rows, the due row lit, with a pass-style card for the current dose.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: time-ordered doses and held alerts suit reminders; loses on identification, since patients know pill packs better than gate boards.
options.risk: Can feel like travel, not care, if the board metaphor leads.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Every dose a stamp-sized cell in a dense numbered grid.
options.viewport: A packed grid of tiny dose cells.
options.risk: Far too dense for older or low-vision patients.
options.case: Loses both axes: patients do not know this world and density fights clarity.
options.kept: One pen-ring marks the active item; finished items stay visible, struck through.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size, raked glass slides on a lit goldenrod bed.
options.risk: Raked shapes and one type size hurt low-vision reading.
options.case: Loses both axes: unfamiliar and hard to read for this audience.
options.kept: State lives in a fixed cell: filled holds, empty is done.

options.label: Zoo and Gardens Guide Map
options.thesis: Swelling lobes of flat colour, one dominating each screen.
options.viewport: A green lobe filling the screen.
options.risk: Playful overshoot motion unsettles anxious patients.
options.case: Loses both axes: leisure-park tone undercuts medical trust.

options.label: Bitmap Type Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel display type at poster scale.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over dense columns.
options.risk: Pixel type is hard to read for low vision.
options.case: Loses both axes: novelty type defeats legibility.
options.kept: Strict size steps of one face carry the hierarchy.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs every glyph on the page.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with axis sliders.
options.risk: A type specimen says nothing about medicine.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to patients or doses.
options.kept: One control remaps the whole page live (the text-size setting).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean medication app like Apple Health: white rows, blue accent, red for alerts.
canonCard.viewport: A list of today's medicines with times and a Take button on the due one.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every medication app by design.
